symbols.name: useAbEdgeSwipe
symbols.description: 🤏 useAbEdgeSwipe — open a side drawer with an edge swipe (drawer spec §2 / §3): - 🧱 the press starts in a 24px zone on that edge of the app box (16px in on iOS standalone) - ↔️ it commits past 30% of the drawer width or above 0.5px/ms toward the middle; slower or shorter does nothing - 🎠 ignored inside things that scroll sideways (code blocks, carousels) and [data-ab-no-edge-swipe] - 🧭 a mostly vertical move is a scroll, not a swipe - 📱 iOS Safari's own back gesture starts at the very screen edge and takes the touch before the page sees it, so the two don't fight; in standalone mode the 16px inset leaves that edge to the system - 👆 touch uses touch events (non-passive touchmove only during an edge press, preventDefault only once it's sideways), so Android Chrome's pointercancel-on-pan can't swallow it The drawer opens on release (it doesn't follow the finger), then slides in with its normal 200ms motion.
symbols.signature: useAbEdgeSwipe({ edge, onOpen, enabled = true, width = 320, pointerTypes = ['touch', 'pen'], maxWidth }: UseAbEdgeSwipeOptions): void

rows.name: { edge, onOpen, enabled = true, width = 320, pointerTypes = ['touch', 'pen'], maxWidth }

symbols.name: AB_SWIPE
symbols.description: 🎚️ the spec numbers (drawer-spec.md "Gestures" + "Edge zones")
symbols.value:
{
  ratio: 0.3, // 📏 30% of the travel / sheet / drawer width
  velocity: 0.5, // ⚡ px per ms: at or above this a release counts as a fast swipe
  edge: 24, // 🧱 edge zone width (px) for the side-drawer swipes
  standaloneInset: 16, // 📱 iOS standalone: the zone starts 16px in (the system owns the very edge)
  slop: 8, // 🫳 px of movement before a press becomes a drag (taps stay taps)
  secondSwipe: 24, // ✌️ px: after a gentle return to S1, a swipe down this long closes (the "second swipe")
}

symbols.description: 🗺️ getAbDrawerHost — the box a drawer of scope is clipped by: the scope element that contains from (so two layouts on a page each get their own), else the first one in the document, else <body>. Effects / handlers only (it reads the DOM).

symbols.name: resolveAbSheetRelease
symbols.description: 🧲 resolveAbSheetRelease — where a released bottom sheet goes (spec §1 "Gestures"): - ⬆️ up past 30% of S1→S2, or faster than 0.5px/ms → full - ⬇️ at S2: fast (≥ 0.5px/ms) or past 30% of the sheet → closed; a gentle drag → back to partial - ⬇️ at S1: fast or past 30% of S1 → closed; after a gentle return from S2 any real swipe down (≥ 24px) → closed - otherwise it springs back to where it was
symbols.signature: resolveAbSheetRelease({ from, dy, velocity, partialHeight, fullHeight, returned = false }: AbSheetReleaseInput): AbSheetRelease

rows.name: variant
rows.description: 🧭 0.1.6 (G17): 'panes' = the docs shell (4 breakpoints, rail, overlay aside). Default keeps the old layout.

rows.name: railCollapsed
rows.description: 🧷 0.1.6: collapse the sidebar to the icon rail (tablet and up, variant="panes").

rows.name: tabletHeader
rows.description: 📟 0.2.0 (P2): 'main' = on tablet (768–1179) hide the app header and show AbMainLayout's mainHeader instead (hidden at other widths). Default 'header'.

rows.name: mobileHeader
rows.description: 📱 0.2.1: 'main' = below 768px hide the app header and show AbMainLayout's mainHeader as the 56px mobile bar (16px inset, 1px divider). Default 'header' (unchanged).

rows.name: mainHeaderAt
rows.description: 📌 0.2.3: 'all' = AbMainLayout's mainHeader stays visible at EVERY width (with mobileHeader="main" it is the mobile bar below 768px, and an extra header row under the app header from 768px), so ONE header can carry e.g. a counter row everywhere instead of rendering it twice. Default 'auto' (unchanged).

rows.name: asideBelow
rows.description: 📑 0.2.3: where the aside pane goes below the laptop breakpoint (< 1180px). 'hidden' (default) = unchanged: an overlay sheet / right drawer opened by the TOC button. 'inline-before-main' = the SAME aside element (rendered once, no duplicate DOM) sits in the flow above the main pane (mobile: aside · main · bottom bar; tablet: sidebar | aside over main), e.g. the Welcome live playground. For any other spot, render your aside content into your own node (a portal) and keep 'hidden'. 📜 0.2.3 'inline-in-main' = the SAME aside element joins the main pane's ONE scroller below 1180px, after the main header (and after AbMainLayout's asideAnchor block when given): v6 phone order header bar · counter · scene · text · nav, nothing pinned. ≥ 1180px: the normal side pane.

rows.name: surface
rows.description: 🎠 0.2.3: 'page' sets data-ab-surface="page": with theme ≥ 0.3.7 every pane paints the v6 page surface (--ab-color-welcome-pane / -main) instead of the white ≥ 1920px light panes. Default: none.

rows.name: asideDrawerAt
rows.description: 📱 0.2.3: 'mobile' = below 768px the aside is a RIGHT DRAWER (out of the page flow until opened by AbAsideDrawerTrigger / useAbPage().setAsideOpenOnMobile(true)), while asideBelow="inline-in-main" still puts the SAME element inline at 768–1179px. Rendered once. Default: none (unchanged).

rows.name: mainBarPin
rows.description: 📌 0.2.3: mirror of AbMainLayout mainBarPin on the root (either one pins the bar).

rows.name: overlays
rows.description: 🧰 0.1.6: render the legacy #backdrop / #menus / #dialogs / #toasts / progress / canvas layers. Default: on for variant="default", off for "panes" (the shell brings its own menus and dialogs).

symbols.name: UseAbScrollSpyOptions
symbols.description: 🎛️ Options for useAbScrollSpy.

rows.name: rootMargin
rows.description: 📏 IntersectionObserver rootMargin. Default: AB_SCROLL_SPY_ROOT_MARGIN for the window (64px sticky bar), AB_SCROLL_SPY_PANE_ROOT_MARGIN when root is set (a pane has no bar inside it).

rows.name: threshold
rows.description: 🎚️ IntersectionObserver threshold (default 0).

rows.name: root
rows.description: 🪟 scroll container (default: the viewport). With core 0.1.6 panes pass useAbPage().mainScrollElement (G55).

rows.name: lastAtBottom
rows.description: 🔚 at the bottom of the root the **last** id wins, even if it can't reach the top (default true).

rows.name: enabled
rows.description: 🔌 turn the spy off without unmounting (default true).

rows.name: initialId
rows.description: 🧭 id to report before anything intersects (default: the first id).

symbols.name: useAbScrollSpy
symbols.description: 🔭 useAbScrollSpy — which section of the page is "current" for an "On this page" TOC. - 👀 One IntersectionObserver watches every id; the **first id in document order** that is visible wins. - 📌 When nothing is visible (between two long sections) the last active id is kept, so the rail never blinks. - 🔚 When the root (or the page) is scrolled to the bottom, the last id wins: short last sections still light up. - 🖥️ SSR / no IntersectionObserver: returns initialId (default the first id) and never throws.
symbols.signature: useAbScrollSpy(ids: readonly string[], options: UseAbScrollSpyOptions = {}): string | null

symbols.name: ScrollToAbSectionOptions
symbols.description: 🎛️ Options for scrollToAbSection.

rows.name: offset
rows.description: 📏 pixels to leave above the section (e.g. the sticky app bar height). Default 0.

rows.name: container
rows.description: 📜 the scroll container (e.g. useAbPage().mainScrollElement, the panes main, G55). Default: the window. Effective fallback when omitted: null. Not a declared initializer.

rows.name: root
rows.description: Effective fallback when omitted: null. Not a declared initializer. Alias of container.
rows.deprecated: 0.1.7: use container (same thing; kept as an alias).

rows.name: updateHash
rows.description: 🔗 also update the URL hash with history.replaceState (no jump). Default true.

symbols.name: scrollToAbSection
symbols.description: 🧭 scrollToAbSection — scrolls to #id, **smoothly unless the user prefers reduced motion** (then instant). Returns false when the element doesn't exist (or on the server).

symbols.name: AB_SCROLL_SPY_ROOT_MARGIN
symbols.description: 📏 Default margin: ignore the top 64px (sticky app bar) and the bottom 60% (so the section near the top wins).

symbols.name: AB_SCROLL_SPY_PANE_ROOT_MARGIN
symbols.description: 📏 Default margin with a root (core 0.1.6 panes main): the bar sits outside the pane, only the bottom 60% is ignored.

symbols.name: getAbMainScroller
symbols.description: 📜 getAbMainScroller — the element that scrolls the page content: the core panes main pane when present, else null (= the window). Pass from (e.g. the heading) to pick the pane that contains it. Use it as useAbScrollSpy({ root }) / scrollToAbSection(id, { container }). ⚠️ Call it only in an effect or an event handler, **never during render**: it reads the DOM, so a render call returns null on the server and the element on the client (hydration mismatch). (nit)
symbols.note: Exported from ab-nextjs-components/ab-toc. It is not a core export.
